cards.explanation: The answer is lips free of deceit. David says his prayer comes from “…lips free of deceit.” (Psalm 17:1) No spin, no sales pitch, no fancy wrapping paper. He's telling it to the LORD straight, friends, and I like that.

The answer is that God found no evil in him. David says, “You have tested me and found no evil…” (Psalm 17:3) He's saying the LORD tried his heart and even visited him in the night. I think David is laying his whole heart out where God can see it.

The answer is True. David says, “I have resolved not to sin with my mouth.” (Psalm 17:3) He made up his mind about his mouth. Honestly, my mouth could use a resolution like that on a day when I'm hungry.

The answer is False. David says, “My steps have held to Your paths; my feet have not slipped.” (Psalm 17:5) Feet that didn't slip, steps that held. That's a man walking steady, and he's not tiptoeing like the floor is wet.
The word is answer. David says, “I call on You, O God, for You will answer me.” (Psalm 17:6) He isn't hoping the line picks up, friends. He's sure God will answer him.

The answer is those who seek refuge from their foes. David says God saves by His right hand “…those who seek refuge from their foes.” (Psalm 17:7) The people he names are the ones who seek refuge. The trouble they're seeking refuge from is their foes.

The answer is the wicked who attack him. David asks to be hidden “…from the wicked who assail me, from my mortal enemies who surround me.” (Psalm 17:8-9) Those are the ones he names. He's asking for shelter from their attack.

The answer is False. David says, “They have closed their callous hearts; their mouths speak with arrogance.” (Psalm 17:10) Arrogance is what comes out of those mouths, bakers. Humility isn't in that picture at all.
The word is surround. David says, “They have tracked us down, and now surround us…” (Psalm 17:11) They found him, and now they're all around him. That's why he's asking God for shelter.

The answer is a lion greedy for prey. David compares them to “…a lion greedy for prey, like a young lion lurking in ambush.” (Psalm 17:12) Both pictures are lions, one hungry and one waiting in hiding. That tells you how David sees the danger around him.

The answer is bring them to their knees. David prays, “Arise, O LORD, confront them! Bring them to their knees…” (Psalm 17:13) He asks the LORD Himself to step in, friends. David isn't handing this one to anybody else.
The answer is True. David says, “May You fill the bellies of Your treasured ones…” (Psalm 17:14) He prays for God's treasured ones to be filled. A full belly is a good thing to ask the LORD for.

The answer is their abundance. David prays that the treasured ones and their sons are satisfied, “…so they leave their abundance to their children.” (Psalm 17:14) The prayer reaches past one generation. He's asking for plenty to be passed down.

The word is satisfied. David says, “when I awake, I will be satisfied in Your presence.” (Psalm 17:15) After all the lions and the surrounding and the crying out, his prayer closes on being satisfied in God's presence, friends.
